text.p: Productivity Technologies Corp on Tuesday said it expected stronger earnings in the third and fourth quarters of its fiscal year compared with profit in the first two quarters.

The expectation for higher earnings in the last two quarters of the year ending June 30 "is based on more product throughput and manufacturing equipment with improved margins," the company said in a statement.
Its $18.5 million backlog of orders on December 31 was for equipment expected to yield higher margins than the backlog processed by the company in the first two quarters, it said.
Earlier, the company said its second-quarter net income fell 14 percent to $107,812 from $125,562 in the year-earlier period. Income from operations rose to $344,093 from $330,283.
Consolidated sales rose 17 percent to $9.39 million from $8.02 million.
The decline in net income was primarily because of increased debt and higher one-time expenses associated with the development of a new line of destacking products, the company said.
Productivity Technologies is a supplier of equipment used to automate metal-stamping lines in the automotive and appliance industries.
